papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine for Depression With Anxiety and Somatic Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
papers.authors: Feng Y, Liu W
papers.abstract: ObjectiveSomatic symptoms are often linked with depression and anxiety, making diagnosis difficult and limiting treatment effectiveness. Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine has been studied as a complementary approach; however, its efficacy and safety have not been systematically evaluated. This review and meta-analysis examined the effectiveness and safety of integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine in patients diagnosed with depression with or without comorbid anxiety and somatic symptoms.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. English-language studies published from 2014 to 2026 were searched in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus. Randomized controlled trials comparing integrated therapy with control interventions were included. The primary outcome was depression severity assessed by HAMD scores. Secondary outcomes included anxiety symptoms, somatic symptoms, and adverse events. A random-effects model was used, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic.ResultsEleven studies met review criteria. Integrated therapy significantly reduced depression severity compared with the standard Western medicine control condition (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.71 to -3.19; I2 = 59%). Anxiety symptoms were also significantly reduced (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.65 to -3.26; I2 = 50%). Somatic symptoms, including sleep disturbances and pain-related outcomes, improved but were assessed descriptively because of reporting variability. Adverse events were lower or similar in combined treatment groups, indicating a favorable safety profile. Funnel plot analysis suggested minimal publication bias.ConclusionIntegrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine was associated with greater improvements in depression and anxiety symptoms than the included control interventions, which comprised Western medicine alone, placebo/sham interventions, or usual care, while showing generally good tolerability. However, given the methodological limitations, heterogeneity of comparator conditions, and low certainty of the available evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Acupuncture versus reflexology for cancer-related pain in palliative care: a pragmatic study.
papers.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
papers.authors: Samuels N, Seckbach E, Ben-Arye E
papers.abstract:
Integrative oncology (IO) provides evidence-based therapies addressing symptoms and wellbeing. We compared acupuncture to reflexology for pain and wellbeing among oncology patients.
This comparative effectiveness observational study examined patients undergoing 8 weekly IO treatments with either acupuncture or reflexology, based on patient preference. Symptoms and wellbeing were assessed using the Measure Yourself Concerns and Wellbeing (MYCAW); Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS); and European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30).
Of 136 treated patients, 45 (33.1%) chose acupuncture and 91 (66.9%) reflexology. Most were female (111;81.0%), aged 59.7±14.3 years, and Jewish (125; 91.9%). A third had metastatic cancer (45; 34.4%), most undergoing adjuvant treatment (63; 48.1%). Metastatic disease was more prevalent in reflexology-treated patients (OR=2.86; p=0.018; 95%CI=1.20-6.84). Both treatments were associated with within-group improvement on ESAS fatigue, appetite; Total ESAS; and EORTC fatigue, pain and physical, emotional and social function. Only acupuncture was associated with within-group improvement on ESAS pain; and only reflexology on ESAS wellbeing and EORTC Global Health/QoL, nausea/vomiting and insomnia. Reflexology showed a between-group advantage for appetite and cognitive function.
Both acupuncture and reflexology were associated with reduced within-group EORTC pain and ESAS and EORTC fatigue and appetite, physical, emotional and social function; only acupuncture with reduction of ESAS pain; and only reflexology improved wellbeing, somnolence and insomnia, with a between-group advantage for EORTC appetite and cognitive function. Further research is needed to confirm the findings within larger and more diverse patient populations.

papers.title: Potential Mechanisms of N-Methyltyramine in Multitarget Regulation of Mental Disorders via the GPCR-cAMP Pathway.
papers.authors: Zijian W
papers.abstract: N-Methyltyramine (NMT) is a tyramine derivative widely distributed in citrus plants and the traditional Chinese medicine Zhishi. Pharmacological studies have confirmed that NMT directly binds to the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2; Ki = 31.3µM), inhibits forskolin-induced cAMP accumulation (EC₅₀ ≈ 4µM, Emax = 89%), and dose-dependently antagonizes quinpirole-mediated β-arrestin2 recruitment, exhibiting G protein-biased agonistic properties. Meanwhile, NMT activates the human trace amine-associated receptor 1 (hTAAR1; EC₅₀ ≈ 2µM) to increase cAMP, possesses α₂-adrenergic receptor antagonistic activity (IC₅₀ = 5.53µM), and exhibits blood-brain barrier permeability (logPe = -5.16cm/s). Based on these multi-target receptor profiles, NMT may participate in the regulation of central monoaminergic neurotransmission via the GPCR-cAMP signaling axis, providing a new multi-target lead compound direction for research on neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, depression, and drug addiction. Notably, evidence for direct activation of β₂-adrenergic receptors by NMT remains insufficient, and its therapeutic effects and downstream signal integration mechanisms require NMT-specific experimental validation.

papers.title: Dahuang Fuzi decoction attenuates renal fibrosis via suppression of the NF-κB pathway.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Niu Z, Guo M, Sun W, Li R
papers.abstract:
Renal fibrosis is a key pathological process in chronic kidney disease with limited treatment options. Dahuang Fuzi Decoction (DFT), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula, shows therapeutic potential, but its anti-fibrotic mechanism remains unclear.
The anti-fibrotic effect of DFT was assessed in a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rat model via histopathological examination and renal function tests. The underlying mechanism was investigated using an integrated strategy which included serum pharmacology with drug-containing serum from treated rats, network pharmacology to screen bioactive compounds and predict targets, and in vitro validation in angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated NRK-52E cells, with a focused analysis of the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway.
DFT treatment ameliorated renal injury, reduced collagen deposition, and improved biochemical parameters in UUO rats. DFT-containing serum attenuated Ang II-induced fibrotic responses in cells. Bioinformatics and experimental validation identified the NF-κB pathway as a key target. DFT suppressed p65 nuclear translocation and downstream target gene expression in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated NRK-52E cells, and pharmacological activation of this pathway reversed the protective effects of DFT.
DFT alleviates renal fibrosis, at least in part by inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway, as validated in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated tubular epithelial cells, providing a pharmacological basis for its clinical application.

papers.title: Qu's Formula 1 for Anxiety and Depression in PCOS: A Computational Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.authors: Liu C, Hu W, Zhou J, Wang F, Zhang R, Qu F
papers.abstract: Qu's Formula 1 (QUF1), a patented Chinese herbal medicine, has shown clinical potential in alleviating anxiety and depression in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). This study aimed to investigate potential molecular mechanisms associated with QUF1 using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Active constituents and potential therapeutic targets of QUF1 were identified using TCMSP and BATMAN-TCM, while PCOS-, anxiety-, and depression-related targets were retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and DrugBank. Overlapping targets were used to construct a herb-constituent-target network, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses to identify relevant pathways. Molecular docking and 100 ns MD simulations were subsequently used to assess predicted interactions and structural stability between selected constituents and key targets. A total of 76 common targets were identified at the intersection of QUF1 and the disease-related target sets. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis highlighted ALB, TNF, AKT1, IL-6, and ESR1 as key network targets, while KEGG enrichment identified the PI3K-Akt, HIF-1, and FoxO signaling pathways among the relevant pathways. Molecular docking and MD simulations further indicated favorable predicted interactions and generally stable structural behavior for the selected compound-target complexes. These findings support a computational hypothesis that QUF1 may act through a multi-compound, multi-target network associated with inflammatory regulation in PCOS-related anxiety and depression. The results provide a theoretical framework for subsequent experimental and pharmacokinetic validation.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanism of Ganoderic Acid B for Insomnia Based on Metabolomics, Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: Wan C, Du Y, Miu J, Chen P, Han Y, Sun S et al.
papers.abstract: Objective: Ganoderma lucidum, a fungus of the genus Ganoderma in the family Polyporaceae, is often used in traditional medicine for the treatment of insomnia and amnesia, etc. Ganoderic acid B, a characteristic lanostane-type triterpenoid isolated from Ganoderma lucidum, has been preliminarily verified to possess mild sedative activity in existing studies. This study aims to explore the potential regulatory mechanism of Ganoderic acid B against PCPA-induced insomnia-like damage via multiple preclinical research strategies, and provide preliminary molecular and experimental clues for subsequent basic mechanistic research of this compound. Methods: Taking Ganoderic acid B as the research object, we established a PCPA-induced mouse insomnia model and evaluated its protective effects on insomnia-associated pathological lesions through behavioral assays, biochemical detection, and cerebral histopathological observation. Subsequently, UHPLC-MS/MS serum metabolomics analysis was performed to screen characteristic biomarkers and pivotal metabolic pathways linked to insomnia pathology. Next, compound and disease target databases were combined to obtain overlapping targets correlated with the alleviation of insomnia lesions by Ganoderic acid B; network pharmacology analyses, including GO and KEGG enrichment, were implemented to screen core hub targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to preliminarily verify the binding interaction between Ganoderic acid B and these targets. Finally, an in vitro CORT-triggered HT22 neuronal injury model was adopted for experimental validation, and Western blot assays were conducted on mouse brain tissue to detect the expression of core regulatory proteins. Results: In vivo experiments showed Ganoderic acid B alleviated weight loss and abnormal behaviors, raised serum 5-HT and GABA, and lowered DA and NE in PCPA insomnia model mice. Metabolomics screened six key insomnia-related serum markers, with phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthesis as the core pathway. CCK-8 assays showed that 4 and 8 μM Ganoderic acid B had no cytotoxicity and relieved CORT-induced neuronal injury, while 16 μM inhibited HT22 cell viability. Network pharmacology identified six core regulatory proteins (EP300, HDAC1, ESR1, IL-6, TNF, NCoR1) mediating Ganoderic acid B's protective effects against insomnia lesions, with Pathways in cancer enriched. Molecular docking verified stable binding between Ganoderic acid B and these targets. Western blot results indicated Ganoderic acid B downregulated NCoR1, EP300, HDAC1, IL-6, and TNF and upregulated ESR1 expression Conclusion: Ganoderic acid B alleviates PCPA-triggered behavioral abnormalities, neurotransmitter disturbance, and hippocampal neuronal injury in mice via multitarget, multipathway synergistic regulation of NCoR1, EP300, ESR1, HDAC1, IL-6, and TNF, and restores the disrupted phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthetic network. This work offers preliminary preclinical and molecular evidence to clarify how Ganoderic acid B relieves insomnia-related pathological injuries.

papers.title: Synergistic Inhibition of Spinal TRPV1 Signaling by Combined Eye Acupuncture and Electroacupuncture Alleviates Inflammatory Pain in a Rat Model of Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Chen S, He Y, Que B, Liang Z, Chen X, Li S et al.
papers.abstract:
Chronic pain caused by knee osteoarthritis (KOA) remains inadequately managed by safe, non-pharmacological therapies. Although acupuncture is recommended for KOA pain by clinical guidelines, the efficacy of single-modality acupuncture remains modest, and the synergistic mechanisms of combining different acupuncture modalities are poorly understood.
To determine whether combining eye acupuncture (EAp) with electroacupuncture (EA) produces greater analgesia in a rat KOA model via regulation of TRPV1 signaling in the spinal dorsal horn (SDH) and dorsal root ganglia (DRG).
Thirty-six Sprague-Dawley rats (19 males, 17 females) were randomized into sham, model, EA, and combination (EA + EAp) groups (n = 9 per group, each containing 4-5 rats of each sex). KOA was induced by anterior cruciate ligament transection combined with medial meniscectomy. After 7 days of intervention, mechanical and thermal pain thresholds were assessed. Serum concentrations of PGE2, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α were quantified by ELISA. TRPV1 expression in SDH and DRG was detected by immunofluorescence and Western blot.
Combination treatment significantly elevated pain thresholds and was associated with reduced levels of all four cytokines compared to the model and EA groups (P < 0.05 or P < 0.01). On day 7, the combination group showed a 2.2-fold increase in MWT compared to the model group (18.7 ± 2.6 g vs 8.5 ± 1.9 g, P < 0.001) and a 31.7% increase compared to the EA group (P < 0.01). Immunofluorescence showed the lowest TRPV1/DAPI fluorescence intensity ratio in the combination group in both DRG and SDH (P < 0.01 vs model; P < 0.05 vs EA). Western blot showed that combination therapy was associated with markedly lower total TRPV1 and phosphorylated TRPV1 (p-TRPV1) protein levels compared with the model and EA groups, with consistent trends in male and female rats.
Combined EAp and EA exert synergistic anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects in KOA rats, which are associated with downregulation of TRPV1 signaling in the SDH and DRG.

papers.title: Genotoxic evaluation of chemical fractions of Cymbopogon citratus (DC) Stapf using plasmid assay.
papers.authors: Carrasco-Alfonso M, Fuentes-León F, Sánchez-Hechavarría L, Rodríguez-Hernández C, Sánchez-Lamar Á, Francioso A
papers.abstract:
Cymbopogon citratus (DC.) Stapf is a medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine in Africa, Asia and Latin America, mainly consumed as aqueous decoctions or infusions to treat fever, colds, cough, gastrointestinal disorders, hypertension, inflammation and anxiety. Despite its extensive traditional use, information on the genotoxic and oxidative effects of its individual chemical fractions remains limited.
The DNA strand breaks and oxidative effects of the aqueous, butanolic and essential oil fractions obtained from the aqueous extract of C. citratus were evaluated using an ex vivo purified pCMUT plasmid DNA model. Cleavage was analyzed after short- and long-term exposure, and oxidative damage was assessed using formamidopyrimidine-DNA glycosylase (FPG). Phytochemical characterization of the aqueous and butanolic fractions was performed by HPLC-HR-MS/MS.
None of the fractions induced plasmid cleavage after 30 min of exposure. However, the aqueous fraction caused significant DNA strand breaks after prolonged incubation. Oxidative DNA damage was detected with the aqueous and essential oil fractions, whereas the butanolic fraction showed no detectable oxidative or breaking effects. Phytochemical analysis revealed qualitative and quantitative differences between fractions, particularly in phenolic acids and flavonoids.
The aqueous fraction of C. citratus exhibits a higher genotoxic and pro-oxidant potential under prolonged exposure, while the butanolic fraction presents a safer profile under the evaluated conditions. These findings highlight the importance of fraction-specific toxicological assessment to support the safe traditional and pharmacological use of C. citratus.
papers.title_ko: 시트로넬라풀(Cymbopogon citratus) 화학 분획의 유전독성 평가: 플라스미드 분석

summary.question: 시트로넬라풀의 수용성, 부탄올성, 정유 분획이 DNA 손상과 산화적 독성을 보이는지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: 추출물의 수용성, 부탄올성, 정유 분획을 pCMUT 플라스미드 DNA 모델에 적용해 단기·장기 노출 후 절단과 FPG 기반 산화 손상을 ex vivo로 분석하고, 수용성과 부탄올성 분획은 HPLC-HR-MS/MS로 성분을 확인하였다.

summary.limitations: 세포나 임상 대신 플라스미드 기반 ex vivo 모델을 사용해 실제 인체 노출과 독성을 그대로 반영하기 어렵다.

papers.title: Acupuncture combined with transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation for chronic postpartum insomnia comorbid with emotional disorders: a case report.
papers.authors: Lyu Q, Ju-Lai-Ti RY, Wang SM, Jing MM, Li YF, Zhou E et al.
papers.abstract: Postpartum women constitute a vulnerable population in whom insomnia comorbid with emotional disorders such as anxiety and depression is disproportionately prevalent, attributable to hormonal fluctuations, environmental changes, and social role transitions. This comorbidity significantly increases their long-term risk of mental health disorders. Given the safety concerns of sedative-hypnotic medications, non-pharmacological therapies are the first-line treatment for this population. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman with chronic postpartum insomnia comorbid with emotional disorders, who provided written informed consent for the publication of her de-identified clinical data and received 4 weeks of combined acupuncture and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) treatment. Clinical assessments were performed at baseline, week 2, week 4 (end of treatment), and week 8 (4-week post-treatment follow-up) using validated scales including the PSQI, ISI, and HAMA, among others. After 4 weeks of treatment, the patient demonstrated significant improvements in objective sleep quality and anxiety symptoms, while subjective insomnia perception and depressive symptoms remained partially unresolved. Notably, all clinical outcomes continued to improve to near-normal levels during the follow-up period without any additional intervention, and no adverse events were recorded. This case demonstrates that combined acupuncture and taVNS is a safe and effective intervention for chronic postpartum insomnia comorbid with emotional disorders, with a favorable sustained therapeutic effect after treatment cessation, offering a valuable alternative for non-pharmacological management in this population.

papers.title: Harmonizing Vietnamese traditional and western medicine: a digital health blueprint and the IMKE architectural framework.
papers.authors: Nguyen Thi Dieu A, Le Ngoc H
papers.abstract: The concurrent use of traditional and Western medicine is a global healthcare reality. In countries like Vietnam, dual-paradigm clinical guidelines actively mandate integrated treatments for high-prevalence chronic diseases. However, safe integration at the point of care is severely hindered by data fragmentation, profound epistemological differences, and a critical "shadow pharmacovigilance" crisis regarding underreported herb-drug interactions (HDIs). This paper analyzes the state-of-the-art of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in integrative healthcare and proposes the Integrative Medicine Knowledge Engine (IMKE), a novel architectural blueprint designed to safely bridge Vietnamese traditional medicine (VTM) and Western biomedicine. Shifting from siloed technical models to a clinical-first perspective, the IMKE conceptualizes a three-stage digital health pipeline: (1) advanced medical text mining to digitize unstructured traditional practitioner notes; (2) an Integrative Knowledge Graph (IKG) that maps holistic VTM diagnostic patterns to Western pharmacological databases and ICD-10 standards; and (3) an AI-driven Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for proactive HDI safety monitoring. We illustrate this architectural data flow through three clinical scenarios-Essential Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes, and Rheumatoid Arthritis. These scenarios demonstrate the system's theoretical capacity to retrieve culturally appropriate treatments, identify cross-paradigm therapeutic synergies, and generate explainable, mechanistic safety alerts that augment physician judgment while mitigating clinical alert fatigue. Ultimately, the IMKE framework provides a scalable, culturally inclusive roadmap for digital health. By translating centuries of experiential medical wisdom into an interoperable, computationally safeguarded infrastructure, this blueprint sets the foundation for evidence-based integrative care, future retrospective clinical validation, and enhanced patient safety.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorating Cerebral I/R-Induced Inflammatory Response through the TLR/TRAF6/NF-κB Pathway.
papers.authors: Chen YT, Shan YS, Zhao SN, Cao WP, Pu JF
papers.abstract:
The inflammatory response plays a crucial role in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and may offer a new therapeutic approach for stroke. Electroacupuncture has shown potential in treating cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.
Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to four groups: the sham group, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) group, sham electroacupuncture (SEA) group, and electroacupuncture (EA) group. The SEA and EA groups received 30 min of treatment after 60 min of ischemia. Body weight was measured before and 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Neurological function and infarct volume were assessed 24 h after the MCAO/R procedure. Protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) expression levels of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB were evaluated using western blot and reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The mRNA and protein expression of inflammatory markers was assessed using RT-PCR and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
Compared with the MCAO/R group, the EA group exhibited improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, and down-regulated expression of TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB. Additionally, in the EA group, the mRNA and protein expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) were decreased, while the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) was increased.
Electroacupuncture exerts a neuroprotective effect on MCAO/R, potentially through the modulation of the TLR4, TLR9, TRAF6, and NF-κB pathways. This treatment may reduce the cerebral I/R-induced inflammatory response by influencing the TLR/TRAF/NF-κB signaling pathway.

papers.title: Moxibustion for depression: A meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Li Y, Li M, Sun F, Xie Y, Li X, Yin A et al.
papers.abstract:
Moxibustion, a traditional Chinese medicine therapy, is widely used for various diseases and has recently been applied in treating depression. This study aims to systematically assess the efficacy and safety of moxibustion, either alone or in combination with other therapies, for depression.
We conducted a comprehensive search across 7 databases from their inception to December 20, 2023, focusing on randomized controlled trials that compared moxibustion with sham treatments, no treatment, or conventional therapies. The primary outcomes were the overall effective rate and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores, with adverse reaction incidence as the secondary outcome. Data were analyzed with RevMan 5.4 and Stata 18, with bias risk assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Evidence quality was graded with GRADEpro.
This study included 15 randomized controlled trials with 1510 patients. Meta-analysis results showed that moxibustion, alone or combined with other therapies, was more effective than other treatments for managing depression (relative risk = 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI]: [1.03-1.10], P = .0003). Moxibustion, either alone or in combination with other treatments, significantly reduced Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores compared to other treatments used alone (mean difference = -2.10, 95% CI: [-3.00 to -1.20]), with its efficacy comparable to that of antidepressant medications (mean difference = -0.60, 95% CI [-1.31 to 0.12], P = .10). Additionally, in terms of safety, the incidence of adverse reactions associated with moxibustion alone or in combination with other therapies for depression is relatively low (relative risk = 0.57, 95% CI: [0.39-0.84], P = .005). However, the overall quality of the evidence was assessed as low to very low.
Moxibustion has been shown to alleviate depressive symptoms, particularly when combined with other therapies, offering both enhanced efficacy and safety. However, further high-quality studies are necessary to confirm its effectiveness.

papers.title: Systematic Multi-Model Toxicological Evaluation and Phytochemical Signatures of Carthamus tinctorius L., Scabiosa comosa, and Their Mixture: Acute and 28-Day Oral Toxicity Studies.
papers.authors: Lv W, Zhang C, Xue M, Ma Y
papers.abstract:
Carthamus tinctorius L. and Scabiosa comosa Fisch. ex Roem. & Schult. are traditional medicinal plants used within the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and Traditional Mongolian Medicine (TMM) systems in China. Historically, the dried florets of C. tinctorius are administered as an aqueous decoction, typically at 3-10 g/day, and are prescribed to invigorate blood circulation and resolve blood stasis, whereas the capitula of S. comosa are prepared as a decoction or powder, typically at 6-9 g/day, and are utilized to clear heat and detoxify, with traditional indications for liver and pulmonary febrile diseases. However, comprehensive evaluations of their antioxidant properties and toxicological characteristics, particularly regarding their individual and combined applications, remain limited.
This study aimed to systematically characterize the phytochemical composition, antioxidant capacity, and safety profiles of C. tinctorius, S. comosa, and their combination using multiple extraction strategies and complementary biological models.
Water extracts, ethanol extracts, and sequential water-ethanol extracts were prepared and analyzed by LC-MS/MS and total flavonoid content determination. Their antioxidant capacities were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays. The toxicological profiles were investigated using BRL-3A rat hepatocytes, zebrafish embryo toxicity assays, acute oral toxicity studies in mice, and a 28-day repeated-dose oral toxicity study in Wistar rats.
LC-MS/MS profiling revealed diverse chemical constituents, including phenolic acids, flavonoids, coumarins, and iridoids. Notably, C. tinctorius exhibited the highest total flavonoid content (TFC), and sequential extraction significantly increased TFC compared to single-solvent extractions. In the antioxidant evaluations, S. comosa demonstrated the most potent antioxidant capacity with the lowest EC50 values. Toxicity varied by concentration and extract type, with water extracts displaying the lowest toxicity. While high concentrations induced developmental abnormalities (e.g., mortality, oedema) in zebrafish, rodent models demonstrated high safety. Acute (5000 mg/kg) and 28-day repeated administrations caused no mortality or severe histopathological lesions, yielding only minor body weight and biochemical fluctuations.
The present study provides a systematic chemical and toxicological evaluation of C. tinctorius, S. comosa, and their combination. These extracts exhibited antioxidant potential and favorable safety profiles in multiple experimental models, providing important evidence for their further development as medicinal or functional food-related products.

papers.title: Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction attenuates renal fibrosis and suppresses pyroptosis-associated signaling: insights from integrated transcriptomics and serum pharmacochemistry.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Han Y, Wang J, Du L, Zaid Y, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction (WXD) is traditionally prescribed for chronic kidney disease based on the principle of warming yang and resolving blood stasis. However, whether its anti-fibrotic effects involve inflammation-associated pyroptosis remains unclear.
To evaluate the effects of WXD on renal fibrosis and associated changes in NF-κB- and pyroptosis-related signaling.
Thirty-six male C57BL/6 mice were allocated to six groups and subjected to sham surgery or unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) with or without valsartan or graded doses of WXD. The effects of WXD were further evaluated in TGF-β1/TNF-α-stimulated HK-2 cells. Kidney transcriptomics was integrated with serum pharmacochemistry-based network pharmacology restricted to blood-absorbed constituents. Pharmacological perturbations using necrosulfonamide (NSA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were performed in HK-2 cells.
High-dose WXD reduced serum BUN, renal fibrotic area, and GSDMD-N expression by 24.7%, 27.6%, and 29.1%, respectively, compared with UUO mice (all P < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis showed that WXD reversed UUO-induced activation of NF-κB, TNF, and NOD-like receptor signaling. Integration with serum pharmacochemistry identified 36 blood-absorbed constituents and yielded inflammation-related target and pathway profiles consistent with the transcriptomic findings. WXD reduced the abundance of phosphorylated p65, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-N in vivo and in vitro. NSA partially reproduced, whereas LPS partially counteracted, the protective effects of WXD.
WXD attenuates renal fibrosis in association with reduced NF-κB- and pyroptosis-associated signaling. Integrating transcriptomics with network pharmacology based on blood-absorbed constituents provides a biologically relevant strategy for investigating multi-component traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

papers.title: Acupuncture Combined with Auriculotherapy as Adjunctive Therapy for Hyperemesis Gravidarum: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Hospital Stay, Relapse Rate, and Quality of Life.
papers.authors: Wang X, Zhang L, Chen S, Zeng Y, Zheng J, Wang Q et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the efficacy of acupuncture combined with auricular therapy as an adjunct to standard fluid resuscitation in patients with hyperemesis gravidarum (HG).
A total of 122 HG patients were randomly assigned to the acupuncture combined (AC) group (n=61) or standard fluid (SF) group (n=61). The SF group received conventional fluid replacement alone, while the AC group received acupuncture and auricular therapy in addition to fluid resuscitation. Primary outcomes included the Pregnancy-Unique Quantification of Emesis and Nausea (PUQE) score, the Functional Living Index-Emesis (FLIE) score (total and subscores), serum potassium, length of hospital stay, and recurrence frequency; secondary outcomes included the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) and Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) scores. Within-group changes and between-group differences were analyzed using paired t-tests and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) or Mann-Whitney U tests, respectively.
Both groups exhibited significant within-group improvements in PUQE, FLIE, nausea, vomiting, SAS and SDS scores (all p<0.001), with no meaningful change in serum potassium. Post-treatment between-group comparisons, assessed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline values, showed significant advantages for adjuvant acupuncture combined with auriculotherapy in total FLIE score (adjusted mean difference -4.11, 95%CI -8.15 to -0.07, p=0.046), nausea subscore (adjusted mean difference -2.11, 95%CI -4.01 to -0.22, p=0.029), SAS (adjusted mean difference -1.04, 95%CI -2.07 to -0.01, p=0.049) and SDS (adjusted mean difference -1.61, 95%CI -3.12 to -0.10, p=0.037), but no significant differences in PUQE, vomiting subscore or serum potassium. The AC group had a shorter median hospital stay (4 vs 6 days, p=0.041) and lower recurrence frequency (0.15 ± 0.441 vs 0.39 ± 0.759, p=0.048). The proportion of participants with recurrence was 11.48% in the AC group and 24.59% in the SF group, with no significant difference (p=0.068).
While standard fluid resuscitation effectively relieves the core symptoms of HG, adjunctive acupuncture combined with auriculotherapy provided additional benefits regarding quality of life, psychological status, hospital stay, and recurrence frequency, although no significant intergroup difference was observed in post-treatment PUQE scores or the proportion of patients experiencing HG recurrence. This combined intervention may serve as a safe and valuable adjunctive strategy for HG management. Further sham-controlled trials are required to distinguish specific treatment effects from non-specific contextual factors.

papers.title: Implementation rules and research status of acupuncture therapy for anxiety disorders.
papers.authors: Li H, Dong M
papers.abstract: In recent years, the number of studies on acupuncture intervention for anxiety disorders has been gradually increasing, and its application scope in clinical practice has also been expanding. This article intends to review and discuss the combination of common acupoints, specific operation methods, efficacy evaluation indicators, clinical effects and potential mechanisms of action. Available evidence suggests that acupuncture may influence anxiety-related symptoms through multiple neurobiological pathways, including autonomic regulation, neurotransmitter signaling, neuroendocrine regulation, and neuroplasticity-related mechanisms; however, the causal contribution of individual pathways remains incompletely established. However, there are still some shortcomings in relevant studies, such as limited sample size, lack of uniformity in efficacy criteria, and relatively insufficient follow-up time. Future research should pay more attention to the application of evidence-based medicine methods, strengthen the discussion of mechanisms of action, and try to establish more individualized intervention plans.

papers.title: Fraxin alleviates intestinal epithelial cell necrosis in ulcerative colitis by inhibiting the P2Y₁₄R/cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Miao Z, Chen B, Bu S, Yan J, Song Y, Zhao M et al.
papers.abstract: Qinpi is a classic herb used in traditional Chinese medicine to treat diarrhea and dysentery caused by damp-heat. Modern research has confirmed that it can alleviate inflammation of the colonic mucosa in ulcerative colitis (UC). As its core active component, Fraxin exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and intestinal protective effects; however, the specific molecular mechanisms underlying its treatment of UC remain unclear. It is currently known that intestinal inflammation, epithelial necrosis, and disruption of the mucosal barrier are core pathological features of UC. Abnormal activation of the P2Y₁₄R receptor and the downstream cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling pathway is closely associated with the progression of UC; however, there is a lack of clear experimental evidence to confirm whether Fraxin intervenes in UC by regulating this target and pathway. Accordingly, this study took P2Y₁₄R as the core target and systematically investigated the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of Fraxin on UC using in vivo and in vitro models. This study established an in vivo UC mouse model and an in vitro TSZ-induced HT-29 cell injury model. Using H&E staining, IHC, qPCR, ELISA, Western blot, and immunofluorescence techniques, we examined changes in histopathology, inflammatory factors, tight junction proteins, and signaling pathway protein expression. Molecular docking and CETSA experiments were used to validate the targeted binding relationship between Fraxin and P2Y₁₄R, and a P2Y₁₄R overexpression plasmid was employed to verify the functional specificity of the target. The results indicate that Fraxin significantly alleviates inflammatory damage in UC in both in vivo and in vitro models, suppresses abnormal P2Y₁₄R expression, and that P2Y₁₄R overexpression reverses its therapeutic effects. Concurrently, Fraxin downregulates pro-inflammatory factors such as TNF-α, repairs intestinal tight junctions, and improves mucosal permeability. By enhancing CREB-RIPK1 binding to inhibit RIPK1/MLKL pathway activation, it reduces intestinal epithelial necrosis and effectively improves pathological symptoms and disease indices in UC-affected mice. In summary, Fraxin UC damage by antagonizing P2Y₁₄R, regulating the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling axis, inhibiting intestinal epithelial necrosis and inflammatory cascades, and repairing the intestinal mucosal barrier. This study elucidated the core mechanism of Fraxin in treating UC, confirmed that the P2Y₁₄R-cAMP/PKA/CREB axis is a key pathway regulating epithelial damage and inflammatory progression in UC, and provided a novel target and experimental basis for targeted natural medicine therapy for UC.

papers.title: Gomisin A as a multi‑target therapeutic agent: Pharmacological mechanisms, pharmacokinetics and network pharmacology (Review).
papers.authors: Xu J, Shi S, Zhu C, Sui Q, Zhu S, Zhang J et al.
papers.abstract: Gomisin A (GA; C23H28O7) is a principal bioactive dibenzocyclooctadiene lignan derived from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. (Wu Wei Zi), a herb traditionally used in Chinese medicine for its adaptogenic, hepatoprotective and detoxifying properties, particularly in treating fatigue, chronic cough and liver disorders. GA exhibits multi‑target potential against a spectrum of complex diseases. The present study aimed to assess the pharmacological profile, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics (PK) and computational docking of GA, emphasizing its potential as a multi‑target agent. A comprehensive literature search was performed in the PubMed and China National Knowledge Infrastructure database platforms. All mechanistic findings were appraised and stratified by supporting evidence strength, complemented by network pharmacology screening, molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) assessment of representative target complexes. GA exhibits polypharmacological properties, including hepatoprotective, anticancer, cardiovascular‑modulating, neuroprotective and anti‑inflammatory/antioxidant effects, with hepatoprotection representing the most robustly supported preclinical indication. GA modulates key signaling pathways such as the PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK and ErbB receptor family pathways. Network pharmacology analysis identified STAT3, EGFR and mTOR as high‑priority candidate targets. Molecular docking predicted moderate‑to‑strong binding affinity across nine hub proteins, with that of EGFR reaching ‑7.7 kcal/mol. MD simulations further supported the conformational plausibility of the GA‑EGFR, GA‑GSK3β and GA‑STAT3 complexes. PK data identified limited oral bioavailability as a key translational bottleneck. GA holds promise as a multi‑target natural product. Advancing GA toward clinical translation requires addressing PK limitations through advanced delivery systems, alongside orthogonal validation of its predicted targets and preclinical and clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Multiple strategies to improve the therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell‑derived exosome transplantation in ischemic stroke (Review).
papers.authors: Xu Y, Zhou X, Zeng W, Wang J, Zhou L, Li L et al.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a common cause of physical disability and death worldwide. Although it has been indicated that mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) can treat IS through mechanisms such as immunomodulation, angiogenesis and neuroprotection, their clinical application is limited by inherent drawbacks, such as immune rejection risk and tumorigenic potential. Notably, MSC‑derived exosomes (MSC‑Exos) possess advantages, such as a smaller volume, low immunogenicity and low tumorigenicity, enabling therapeutic effects similar to those of the parent cells. Furthermore, MSC‑Exos can carry various bioactive substances and cross the blood‑brain barrier (BBB), thus indicating their potential in the diagnosis, treatment and prognostic assessment of IS. The present review comprehensively elaborates on the principles by which MSC‑Exos may treat IS through mechanisms such as inhibiting inflammatory responses, suppressing apoptosis, promoting angiogenesis, regulating ferroptosis and maintaining BBB integrity. However, the therapeutic efficacy of MSC‑Exo monotherapy is restricted by its low brain bioavailability, short lesion retention time, insufficient in vivo stability and inability to remain at the lesion site for an extended period of time to exert its effect. Furthermore, the review summarizes the recent optimization strategies involving the combination of MSC‑Exos with microRNAs, traditional Chinese medicine, hydrogels, exosome pretreatment and electroacupuncture to enhance the efficacy of MSC‑Exo therapy for IS, and systematically reviews their synergistic therapeutic mechanisms. In addition, the current status of clinical translation, technical breakthrough obstacles and future development directions for MSC‑Exo combination therapies in neurological diseases is outlined, providing a theoretical reference for innovative treatments of IS.

papers.title: Sustainable valorization of traditional Chinese medicine residues via semi-permeable membrane composting: the impacts of nitrogen sources.
papers.authors: Cui D, Gao P, Li C, Wu X, Chen Z, Li A
papers.abstract: Driven by global disease challenges, the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) industry has flourished, however, the massive surge in TCM residues has emerged as a major bottleneck to its sustainable development. Semi-permeable membrane aerobic composting provides a key technology for TCM residue valorization, which typically relies on exogenous nitrogen supplementation to optimize the carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) balance. Nevertheless, a systematic understanding of how differentiated nitrogen sources impact this composting process remains lacking. Herein, this study introduced distinct nitrogen sources as co-substrates for semi-permeable membrane aerobic composting to elucidate their modulation of key physicochemical parameters and microecological succession. The results demonstrated that peanut meal exhibited the optimal composting performance compared to alfalfa meal, soybean meal, and urea. Specifically, its thermophilic phase (> 55°C) persisted for over 7 days, and the organic matter content degraded most rapidly and stably, achieving a reduction rate of 49.8%. At maturity, the ammonium nitrogen (NH4+-N) content and electrical conductivity (EC) dropped to as low as 81 mg/kg and 2606μS/cm, respectively, while the peak total nutrient content reached 5.8%. Meanwhile, the dynamic trend of the ratio of the absorbance at 465 nm to that at 665 nm (E4/E6) aligned with typical aerobic composting patterns, indicating a high degree of humification. Community analysis revealed that Bacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Pseudomonas were the dominant bacterial taxa in the efficient treatments, whereas fungi dominated by Thermomyces, Mycothermus, and Aspergillus were consistently associated with NH4+-N turnover and lignocellulose degradation, these compositional associations suggest a potential contribution of these taxa to compost maturation, which warrants direct functional verification in future studies. Overall, this study provides critical microecological insights and a practical nitrogen optimization strategy for efficient and sustainable TCM residue composting.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology and Bioinformatic Prediction of Five Medicinal-Food Homologous Plants Against the Progression from Chronic Atrophic Gastritis to Gastric Cancer.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.authors: Chen M, Tu H, Yang C, Xu C, Huang Y, He L
papers.abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) progresses through distinct pathological stages to gastric cancer. This computational study employed network pharmacology and bioinformatics to predict the active compounds, targets, and pathways of five medicinal-food homologous plants (Houttuyniae Herba, Mume Fructus, Rhizoma Dioscoreae, Portulacae Herba, and Curcumae longae Rhizoma) against this progression. We identified 28 active compounds and 242 targets from TCMSP. differentially expressed genes from GSE130823 and GSE55696 were integrated with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, yielding 129 candidate targets. Machine learning (LASSO and random forest) prioritized AR, EIF6, GSTM2, and FOSB as potential diagnostic biomarkers distinguishing CAG from cancer. Enrichment analysis predicted involvement of IL-17, TNF, and p53 pathways. Compound-target-pathway network analysis identified quercetin and kaempferol as multi-target compounds. Molecular docking predicted binding affinities ranging from weak-to-moderate for core genes (-2.60 to -5.83 kcal/mol) and moderate-to-strong for inflammatory targets (up to -7.25 kcal/mol for quercetin-TNF). These findings computationally predict candidate mechanisms of these five plants, offering a rationale for future experimental validation and therapeutic development.

papers.title: Update of Korean Medicine Clinical Practice Guidelines for Obesity Management: An Evidence-Based GRADE Approach.
papers.authors: Kim SD, Son MJ, Kim BY, Ko MM, Jegal KH, Kim H et al.
papers.abstract:
Obesity is a major health challenge associated with multiple chronic diseases. Korean traditional medicine (KM) offers diverse therapeutic approaches for obesity management. This study aims to update the Korean Medicine Clinical Practice Guidelines (KMCPGs) by incorporating recent evidence to improve the effectiveness of KM-based obesity care.
The KMCPGs were updated through systematic searches of eight databases for studies published up to December 31, 2022. Evidence quality and recommendation strength were evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
The updated KMCPGs present 20 clinical recommendations, including 7 for KM monotherapies and 13 for KM combination therapies. The recommendations include herbal medicine (A/high), individualized ephedra-containing prescriptions (GPP), acupuncture (B/low), auricular acupuncture (C/low), electroacupuncture (B/low), pharmacopuncture (B/moderate), TEA (C/low), and 13 combination therapies ranging from grade B to C or GPP. Most recommendations focus on anthropometric outcomes, including body weight, BMI, WC, and body fat-related measures.
The update of the KMCPGs underscores the clinical value of KM interventions in obesity management while emphasizing the need for further high-quality studies to strengthen the evidence. Addressing implementation barriers and ensuring regular guideline updates are essential for optimizing clinical application and improving patient outcomes in obesity care.

papers.title: Scale-independent prediction of ribbon and granule quality in dry granulation process based on transfer learning for process transfer.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Zhou L, Zhao Y, Yang Y, Song K, Xie T et al.
papers.abstract: In dry granulation, differences in equipment geometry, compaction mechanisms, and powder flow behavior prevent quality prediction models based on a single device from achieving cross-scale and cross-equipment predictions of ribbon solid fraction (SF) and granule quality. Focusing on ten traditional Chinese medicine "Jichuan decoction" extracts, this study proposes a hybrid transfer learning (TL) framework to perform two-level device transfer for scale-independent prediction of ribbon and granule quality. In the first transfer level, a source domain dataset is constructed using uniaxial compaction experiments, and a target domain dataset using roller compaction experiments; material compression characteristics are extracted via the Johanson model. T-shaped partial least squares regression (T-PLSR) is then introduced for feature alignment and knowledge transfer. In the second transfer level, a Johanson + T-PLSR hybrid model is built, using the compression parameters output by the physical model as input features to jointly predict ribbon solid fraction and density, granule yield, and friability. This hybrid model overcomes the limitation of the Johanson model, which only predicts ribbon solid fraction, achieving end-to-end prediction from material compaction behavior to final granule quality. Validation results show that the prediction accuracy of the hybrid transfer model is significantly superior to pure physical or pure data-driven models, while the inclusion of physical parameters enhances model interpretability and generalization ability.

papers.title: Qingre Chushi decoction ameliorates MC903-induced atopic dermatitis in association with reduced JAK-STAT6 activation and decreased CD206+IL-31+ macrophage abundance.
papers.authors: Meng Y, Ma Y, Liu W, Zhou L, Ma H, Zhu H et al.
papers.abstract: Qingre Chushi Decoction (QRCSD) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used clinically for atopic dermatitis (AD), whereas its immunological basis remains poorly understood. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and associated immune changes of QRCSD in an MC903-induced murine AD model. The chemical profile of QRCSD was characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and four representative marker compounds, including chlorogenic acid, gentiopicroside, baicalin, and glycyrrhizic acid, were quantitatively determined by targeted UPLC-MS/MS in MRM mode for quality control. AD-like lesions were induced in male C57BL/6 J mice by topical MC903 application. Dermatitis severity, scratching behavior, and transepidermal water loss were assessed, while epidermal barrier proteins, pruritogenic mediators, circulating cytokines, and immune-cell profiles were evaluated by histological analysis, immunofluorscence, ELISA, and flow cytometry. QRCSD markedly reduced dermatitis severity, epidermal thickness, TEWL, scratching behavior, and mast-cell infiltration, while restoring filaggrin and involucrin expression and reducing TSLP and IL-31 levels. Circulating IL-4, IL-13, IL-17 A, IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γ, and total IgE were also decreased. Flow cytometry revealed altered T-cell profiles following QRCSD treatment. In the QRCSD-H group, reduced eosinophil and macrophage proportions and decreased CD206+IL-31+ macrophages were observed in lesional skin. Transcriptomic and protein analyses further demonstrated JAK-STAT-associated immune changes, including decreased phosphorylation of JAK1, JAK3, and STAT6, accompanied by reduced Arg1 and CD206 expression. Collectively, QRCSD ameliorated MC903-induced AD and was associated with restored epidermal barrier function, altered systemic and cutaneous immune responses, reduced CD206+IL-31+ macrophage abundance, and decreased JAK-STAT6 pathway activation. These findings provide a biological basis for the immunoregulatory effects of QRCSD in AD.

papers.title: Reporting Quality Assessment of Sham Acupuncture Randomized Controlled Trials for Acupuncture Intervention in Glaucoma.
papers.authors: Lei YF, Huang XY, Xue SY, Cao YJ, Wang XJ, Yang C et al.
papers.abstract:
To systematically evaluate the reporting quality of sham-acupuncture-randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating acupuncture intervention for glaucoma.
A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, SinoMed, and China Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP) for Chinese and English RCTs on acupuncture intervention for glaucoma published from database inception until August 2025. The Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials 2025 (CONSORT), Standards for Reporting Interventions in Clinical Trials of Acupuncture (STRICTA), and the Sham Acupuncture Reporting Guidelines and a Checklist in Clinical Trials (SHARE) were used by the investigators to assess the Overall Quality Score (OQS) of the RCTs that met the pre-defined inclusion criteria. Inter-rater agreement was evaluated using Cohen's κ coefficient.
The systematic search initially identified 1289 relevant records. After a stepwise screening process, it was found that RCTs utilizing sham acupuncture controls were very limited; consequently, only 6 RCTs meeting the pre-defined criteria were ultimately included. According to the CONSORT statement, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 16 items (range: 10-23). Among all CONSORT items, the positive rate for 9 items (21%) was greater than 80%, while for 20 items (48%) it was below 20%. Based on the STRICTA guidelines, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 10.5 items (range: 8-14). For the STRICTA guidelines, the positive rate for 6 items (35%) was greater than 80%, and for 1 item (6%) it was below 20%. According to the SHARE guidelines, the median OQS for the 6 RCTs was 6.5 items (range: 3-10). For the SHARE checklist, 3 items (18%) had a reporting rate >80%, while 10 items (53%) had a rate <20%. The overall average reporting rates based on CONSORT, STRICTA, and SHARE were 39.7%, 62.7%, and 35.1%, respectively.
The current reporting quality of sham acupuncture RCTs on acupuncture intervention for glaucoma is generally suboptimal. There is a particular and urgent need to improve the reporting of detailed information regarding the sham acupuncture control. It is recommended that future relevant RCTs strictly adhere to the CONSORT statement, STRICTA standards, and SHARE checklist for standardized reporting.

papers.title: Integrative therapy with Qinghao Biejia Decoction improves survival after resection of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Chen J, Xia R, Wu M, Wang Y, Liu Y, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is characterized by high postoperative recurrence and limited benefit from conventional adjuvant therapy. Qinghao Biejia Decoction (QHBJD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula, has demonstrated potential anticancer effects. This study investigated the molecular mechanisms of QHBJD in ICC and evaluated its impact on postoperative survival, with a focus on AKT1 expression. In this retrospective study of 60 patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), network pharmacology and bioinformatics analyses were used to identify candidate targets of QHBJD. AKT1 expression was validated by immunohistochemistry in tissue microarrays, and associations between AKT1 expression, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. AKT1 was identified as a key target of QHBJD. In ICC tissues, AKT1 showed predominant nuclear localization, and high nuclear expression was associated with significantly shorter overall survival (OS) (18.4 vs. 25.1 months, p = 0.046). Postoperative adjuvant therapy alone did not significantly improve survival. In contrast, QHBJD-based integrative therapy significantly prolonged OS compared with no treatment (28.8 vs. 14.2 months, p = 0.041) and conventional therapy alone (28.8 vs. 11.2 months, p = 0.001). Among patients with high nuclear AKT1 expression, QHBJD significantly improved both disease-free survival (DFS) (5.95 vs. 2.0 months, p = 0.001) and OS (23.9 vs. 8.0 months, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis confirmed QHBJD-based therapy as an independent protective factor for OS (HR 0.47, p < 0.05). QHBJD-based integrative therapy significantly improves survival in ICC, particularly in patients with high nuclear AKT1 expression, highlighting AKT1 as a potential therapeutic target and candidate prognostic biomarker that warrants further validation.

papers.title: Neuromuscular effects of warm needle acupuncture versus mild moxibustion in knee osteoarthritis: An active-controlled randomized trial.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.authors: Chen G, Su C, Chen X, Zou Y, Chen S, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract: BackgroundKnee osteoarthritis (KOA) is associated with neuromuscular dysfunction and impaired quadriceps activation. This study compared the short-term neuromuscular effects of warm needle acupuncture (WNA) and mild moxibustion (MM).MethodsIn this single-center, assessor- and statistician-blinded randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with KOA were randomized 1:1 to WNA or MM for 4 weeks. Thirty healthy participants provided an exploratory physiological reference at baseline. Co-primary outcomes were isokinetic quadriceps peak torque (PT) and average power (AP). Secondary outcomes included VAS, WOMAC, thigh circumference asymmetry, and surface electromyography (sEMG). Between-group effects were assessed using baseline-adjusted ANCOVA.ResultsAt week 4, WNA showed greater baseline-adjusted improvements than MM in PT (adjusted difference 18.38 N·m, 95% CI 11.69-25.06; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and AP (10.45 W, 95% CI 6.61-14.29; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). VAS and WOMAC also favored WNA, whereas thigh circumference asymmetry was not significantly different. Selected absolute sEMG parameters differed between groups. Credibility and expectancy were comparable, and no serious adverse events occurred.ConclusionsWNA was associated with greater short-term improvements than MM in quadriceps strength, pain, and function. These findings support comparative effectiveness of WNA versus MM but do not isolate thermal-specific, placebo-specific, or expectancy-independent effects.Trial registrationITMCTR2025001238; registered on 16 May 2025 after completion of participant recruitment and follow-up (late/retrospective registration).

papers.title: Effect of Auricular Acupoint Stimulation on Weight in Adults with Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Kim MY, Cho MK
papers.abstract: Objectives: To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of auricular acupoint stimulation for weight reduction and metabolic outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity. Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Methods: Six electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Scopus) were searched from inception to 5 February 2026. The primary outcome was body weight; secondary outcomes included body mass index, waist circumference, and metabolic markers. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. For the primary outcome, a multilevel random-effects model was fitted using restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with small-sample-adjusted cluster-robust variance estimation (CR2) to account for dependent comparisons within studies. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were also conducted. Results: A total of 20 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 14 contributed 15 comparisons to the primary meta-analysis of post-intervention body weight. The pooled effect was Hedges' g = -0.21 (95% CI: -0.42 to -0.01, p = 0.043). Heterogeneity estimates were I2 = 46.6% (95% CI: 8.1-76.8%) and τ2 = 0.06 (95% CI: 0.01-0.21), and the 95% prediction interval ranged from -0.71 to 0.29. Formal subgroup tests and univariate meta-regression yielded p values below 0.05 for publication year, funding status, and quality appraisal score. Sensitivity analyses produced estimates in the same direction, although the confidence interval included the null value in some leave-one-out analyses. Conclusions: The pooled estimate suggested a small reduction in post-intervention body weight with auricular acupoint stimulation, but the prediction interval included the null value, indicating uncertainty in the effect across comparable settings. Further well-designed trials with standardized intervention protocols are needed to clarify the magnitude and consistency of the effect.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of patients with diminished ovarian reserve regarding traditional Chinese medicine treatment: structural equation modelling analysis.
papers.authors: Jiang F, Zheng J, Su L, Cai J, Hong J
papers.abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of patients with diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) regarding Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatments. A cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2023 to August 2024 among patients with DOR to assess their KAP regarding TCM treatments. Data on characteristics and KAP scores were collected via a self-designed questionnaire. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was employed to assess the relationships among the KAP dimensions. A total of 439 valid responses from patients with DOR were included in the final analysis (effective response rate 82.2%). Patients with DOR had a moderate level of knowledge (median [IQR]: 7.00 [5.00-8.00]), generally positive attitudes (median [IQR]: 27.00 [25.00-28.00]), and suboptimal practices (median [IQR]: 31.00 [28.00-33.00]). SEM showed that knowledge had a direct effect on attitude (β = 0.183, P < 0.001) and practice (β = 0.199, P < 0.001), attitude had a direct effect on practice (β = 0.267, P < 0.001), and knowledge indirectly affected practice through attitude (β = 0.049, P = 0.001). Patients with DOR had inadequate TCM knowledge but positive attitudes. Low practice engagement highlights a need for better education to convert attitudes into effective TCM use for managing ovarian decline.

papers.title: Gut microbiome intervention in gut-brain axis and effects on vascular dementia with prospects on non-pharmacological intervention.
papers.authors: Maurya Y, George EA, Roy A, Menon GJ, Harshitha KR, Priyadharshini K et al.
papers.abstract: Vascular dementia (VD) is the second leading cause of cognitive impairment after Alzheimer's disease. Current treatments focus primarily on managing vascular risk factors with no effective interventions for repairing existing brain damage. Recent research underscores a critical link between gut microbiota and brain function through immunological, hormonal and metabolic pathways. Alterations in the gut microbiome influence vascular cognitive impairment via mechanisms such as dysbiosis, induced intestinal permeability, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and blood-brain barrier disruption. Microbial metabolites including butyrate promote neuroprotection and maintain vascular integrity, whereas trimethylamine N-oxide is associated with vascular injury and cognitive decline. Restoration of microbial balance through probiotics, plant-based bioactive compounds and traditional medicines has shown potential in preclinical models for regulating inflammation, improving cognitive outcomes though clinical validation is limited. Non-pharmacological approaches like electro-acupuncture further modulate the microbiome and serotonin regulation. This review explores how changes in gut microbiome influence vascular cognitive impairment and discusses therapeutic strategies for restoring microbial balance. Integrating contemporary and traditional strategies, gut microbiome modulation emerges as a potential therapeutic target for the prevention and management of VD although its clinical applicability remains to be fully established.

papers.title: Integrating at-line nanofractionation platform with GNPS for unveiling neuraminidase inhibitors from ethanolic extract of Smilax china L.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Chen Z, Xu S, Cassas F, Xu L, Wang J, Pang M et al.
papers.abstract: Influenza is a highly transmissible airborne disease that causes acute febrile respiratory illness, ranging from mild fatigue to fatal respiratory failure. Neuraminidase (NA) serves as a primary drug target for both the prevention and treatment of influenza. In this study, an efficient strategy integrating an at-line nanofractionation (ANF) platform with Global Natural Products Social Molecular Networking (GNPS) was employed for the rapid discovery of neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) from the Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Smilax china L. High-throughput screening of a self-constructed TCM extract library revealed that the ethanolic extract of Smilax china L. exhibited over 90% inhibitory activity against oseltamivir-sensitive neuraminidase (NAS), with an IC50 value of 88.78 ± 13.26 μg/mL. The NAS-based ANF platform was then applied, and 21 compounds were prioritized as candidate NAIs based on their association with bioactive ANF fractions. By combining GNPS molecular networking with manual interpretation (mass errors <5 ppm), a total of 97 compounds were annotated (Confidence level II), covering six major classes, including 47 flavonoids, 20 cinnamic acid derivatives, 16 polyphenolic compounds, and 14 others. Among these, the 21 bioactive constituents included chlorogenic acid, astilbin, procyanidin B, and smilaside A. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to explore potential binding interactions and possible structural determinants of candidate binding. The results suggest that these compounds may interact with key residues in the NAS active site, including the 150-loop, the Arg cluster (residues 118, 292, 371), and Glu119. Notably, the 150-loop region is relatively conserved, suggesting a potential structural basis for hypothesizing activity against drug-resistant variants that warrants further experimental investigation. However, docking scores and MD stability are computational predictions and do not establish experimental inhibitory potency; biochemical and antiviral validation is required. The integrated ANF-GNPS platform established in this study provides an efficient and reliable technical approach for the rapid screening and structural annotation of bioactive constituents from TCM. It lays a solid chemical foundation for the discovery of novel NAIs.

papers.title: An integrated FIDI-MS and UPLC-Q-TOF/MS strategy for rapid functional screening and chemical characterization of antioxidants in Polygonum multiflorum.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Xu M, Ma Z, Liu J, Wang L, Ocholi SS, Zhang Z et al.
papers.abstract: A novel integrated strategy combining field-induced droplet ionization mass spectrometry (FIDI-MS) with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF/MS) was developed for the rapid screening and identification of antioxidant constituents in herbal extracts. This approach enables real-time assessment of antioxidant activity within microdroplets and comprehensive compositional characterization of complex matrices. Applied to Polygonum multiflorum extract (PME), the method successfully identified known antioxidants such as 2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucoside (TSG) and revealed additional bioactive phytochemicals. Quantitative FIDI-MS dose-response profiling determined the antioxidant potency of key compounds, with trans-TSG exhibiting superior activity (IC50 = 13.33 ± 1.06 μM) compared to its cis-isomer and emodin. By integrating functional screening, reliable chemical profiling, and targeted quantification, the strategy enabled comprehensive analysis of bioactive constituents in complex herbal samples. Furthermore, the utility of FIDI-MS, when coupled with chromatographic separation and high-resolution mass detection, is underscored as a complementary approach for functional and chemical interrogation of bioactive compounds in botanical matrices.

papers.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
papers.authors: Sim J, Choi KS, Lee DH
papers.abstract:
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms. The primary therapeutic goal of such treatments is to alleviate symptoms while maximizing the functional independence and quality of life of affected individuals. Many complementary and alternative medicine therapies have been reported to have effects on ASD symptoms; however, evidence is insufficient to confirm their clinical effectiveness. Acupuncture has traditionally been used as a complementary intervention to manage various neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including ASD, in East Asia. However, how acupuncture stimulation modulates neural activity at the macroscale level in individuals with ASD remains largely unknown.
This study aims to elucidate disease-related brain alterations and explore the acute neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD and in typically developing (TD) individuals, using a multimodal neuroimaging approach.
This study was designed as a randomized, sham-controlled trial. In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD.
Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026.
ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

summary.limitations: 프로토콜 논문이라 임상적 효과와 안전성에 대한 실제 결과가 아직 제시되지 않았다.

papers.title: TRDMT1-dependent m5C modification of TLR4 mediates the protective effects of Shaoyao decoction in TNBS-induced Crohn's disease.
papers.authors: Deng Y, Wang J, Li M, Xiao G, Pan Y, Tao Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the digestive system with increasing morbidity worldwide. Shaoyao Decoction (SYD), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, has shown therapeutic potential in the treatment of CD. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the protective effects of SYD against 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced CD-like colitis through the tRNA aspartic acid methyltransferase 1 (TRDMT1)/TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.
We used network pharmacology to identify potential targets and related pathways of SYD in the treatment of CD. The CD model was induced by TNBS. Immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and ELISA were employed to detect various cytokines and proteins associated with epithelial barrier, inflammation, apoptosis, and signaling pathway regulation. TLR4 mRNA expression and the 5-methylcytosine (m5C) modification level of TLR4 mRNA were assayed by qRT-PCR and MeRIP-qPCR. TRDMT1 silencing in Caco2 cells and TLR4 knockout (TLR4-/-) mice were used to verify the mechanism by which SYD attenuated CD symptoms.
The TLR4/NF-κB pathway was identified as the core regulatory mechanism. Administration of SYD alleviated TNBS-induced CD-like colitis in mice, as evidenced by the restoration of intestinal mucosal barrier integrity, reduced inflammation, and decreased apoptosis. At the molecular level, SYD reduced the expression of TLR4 and MyD88, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and increased TRDMT1 expression. SYD also enhanced the m5C modification level of TLR4 mRNA. Furthermore, mechanistic studies indicated that TRDMT1 and TLR4 were involved in the protective effects of SYD against CD-like colitis.
SYD can alleviate intestinal inflammation, inhibit apoptosis, and protect the intestinal barrier in the CD model. This protective effect may be mediated through upregulation of TRDMT1, which enhances the m5C modification of TLR4 mRNA, thereby reducing TLR4 expression and suppressing TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling.

papers.title: Salvianolic acid a alleviates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats via SIRT1-mediated inhibition of oxidative stress and inflammation.
papers.authors: Chen Z, Cao Y, Bo H, Yang Y, Liu D, Mao C et al.
papers.abstract:
Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and salvianolic acid A (SAA) is its main bioactive component. Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is common in ischemic heart disease treatment, mainly caused by inflammation and oxidative stress.
To clarify the role of SIRT1 (Sirtuin 1) in SAA's protection against MIRI and the underlying signaling pathways.
The potential targets of SAA and MIRI were identified using SwissTargetPrediction, SEA, TargetNet, GeneCards, OMIM and CTD databases. Gene Ontology Enrichment (GO) and Signaling Pathway Enrichment (KEGG) analyses were performed on these targets. Molecular docking examined SIRT1-SAA interactions. In vivo MIRI models were established by left anterior descending coronary artery ligation in rats, while H9c2 cell hypoxia-reoxygenation (H/R) models served for in vitro studies. Western blotting (WB), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay, immunofluorescence (IF) staining and Quantitative reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were employed to validate the effects of SAA on MIRI therapy. SIRT1 siRNA knockdown confirmed its regulatory role in SAA's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory actions against MIRI.
SAA alleviated MIRI dose-dependently by inhibiting inflammation and oxidative stress, with high binding affinity to SIRT1 (molecular docking). SAA upregulated SIRT1 expression and exerted antiapoptotic effects, activating the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) pathway and suppressing the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathway via SIRT1.
SAA mitigates MIRI-induced oxidative stress and inflammation by activating SIRT1, which regulates the PGC-1α/Nrf2/HO-1 and NF-κB pathways. This confirms SIRT1 as the key upstream mediator of SAA's cardioprotective effects, supporting SAA as a potential therapeutic agent for MIRI.

papers.title: Multi-omics reveals that burdock seed aglycone alleviates renal fibrosis by restoring mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation function.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Wu G, Zhao L, Bo Y, Yang D, Guo J et al.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis (RF), a common pathological process driving chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression to end-stage renal failure, is closely associated with oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Arctigenin (ATG), the main active component of burdock seed, exhibits anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic activities, but its mechanisms in RF treatment remain unclear. Here, we performed integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to identify key targets and pathways of ATG in a unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced rat RF model. Multi-omics enrichment analysis revealed that NDUFS8 and NDUFS2 were the core targets of ATG, with the OXPHOS pathway as the central intersecting pathway. Our results suggest that ATG exerts anti-renal fibrosis effects by targeting the OXPHOS pathway to inhibit excessive reactive oxygen species production and oxidative stress. SIGNIFICANCE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) continues to impose an escalating global health and socioeconomic burden, while renal fibrosis (RF), as the convergent pathological endpoint of virtually all progressive nephropathies, remains the principal determinant of irreversible renal failure and adverse clinical outcomes. Despite extensive efforts to develop antifibrotic therapies, effective clinical interventions remain elusive, largely due to the complex and multifactorial nature of RF pathogenesis. In this study, we employed an integrated multi-omics framework encompassing transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics to systematically decipher the antifibrotic mechanism of arctigenin (ATG), a bioactive natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine. Our findings identify mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation as the pivotal regulatory axis underlying the renoprotective effects of ATG and further establish key catalytic subunits of mitochondrial complex I as its direct molecular targets. Mechanistically, ATG not only restores complex I activity and reprograms mitochondrial energy metabolism but also preserves the intracellular stability and localization of these subunits, thereby preventing their aberrant release-mediated inflammatory activation and disrupting the self-perpetuating cycle linking metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and fibrosis progression. Beyond revealing a previously unrecognized dual mechanism integrating metabolic and inflammatory regulation, this study provides compelling evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction is not merely a secondary consequence of tissue injury but a fundamental driver of fibrotic remodeling. Importantly, our work highlights the translational potential of natural product-based mitochondrial interventions for CKD treatment and supports a broader conceptual shift toward metabolism-centered therapeutic strategies for chronic fibrotic diseases. Given the central role of mitochondrial dysfunction across multiple organs, these findings may also have far-reaching implications for the treatment of systemic fibrosis-related disorders beyond the kidney.
